reason: Stock WebKit has no permission grants: its adapter refuses `permissions` as Unsupported, so `grant` fails there. The matrix row says Strider grants permissions, with no WebKit limit
A grant without an origin is for every origin, which Firefox refuses (`permissions.anyOrigin`: Firefox's BiDi grants to one origin at a time). These tests grant without one
The `permissions` option of a new context grants every origin, which Firefox and WebKit refuse as Unsupported
Upstream runs it on Chromium only: the `storage-access` permission and the Storage Access API are Chromium's

The context accepts the fixture's self-signed certificate with `acceptInsecureCerts`, which Chromium refuses per context (CDP ignores certificate errors browser-wide). The matrix row says Strider has the option, with Chromium refusing true in its notes
Upstream runs it on Chromium only: the `local-fonts` permission and `queryLocalFonts` are Chromium's
Upstream skips it on WebKit: WebKit has no `local-network-access` permission
Upstream runs them on WebKit only, against WebKit's mock capture devices; Chromium and Firefox need a fake device flag and have no camera or microphone permission mapping in the original

The test reads a cross-origin frame's permission and calls its `document.requestStorageAccess()` in the frame's main world, which Strider can't evaluate in a frame (the matrix row says no main-world frame evaluation). A locator into the cross-origin frame doesn't resolve either: `Locator.evaluate` on its `html` element timed out while resolving, so the isolated-world route is closed too. The test isn't ported
